- ⛔ **Anything under `docs/adr/**` is OUT of this card.** That is a governed surface: draft PR only, human merge is the review record, ⛔ never enqueued — so mixing it into a code PR makes the whole PR unlandable by the PM. If the retirement genuinely requires an ADR edit, ✅ **say so in the report and leave it undone**; it becomes its own draft-only PR.

⚠️ **Serial, adjacent semantics:** **#6088 (#5795) is enqueued** and normalises related-list sort through `@object-ui/core`'s `convertSortToQueryParams` — the same sink this card's key feeds. **#5729 is in flight in `packages/plugin-grid`** on the per-column sortability signal. ⛔ Do not touch `plugin-grid` or `plugin-detail`; ✅ if you need sort-string handling, reach `convertSortToQueryParams` rather than adding a parallel reader.

## 裁决 — ruled, and ⛔ not re-openable

Maintainer ruling 2026-08-22 on #4869 (decision-inbox digest, verbatim 「接受所有」): Option A now, **plus** *"the follow-up card for the C half — an ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove retirement of `table.defaultSort` as its own card, not folded into this one."* Option A has landed.

Triage (2026-08-24 01:30Z), verbatim:

> maintainer-directed follow-up … → `domain:ui` + `pm:queue`, Task: ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove retirement of `table.defaultSort`. Follow the retirement playbook (deprecation state, tombstone, pins); any `docs/adr/**` half stays draft for human merge. **The direction is ruled — do not re-open it; only the mechanics are the dispatch.**

⛔ So: do not re-argue whether the key should go. ✅ Decide and execute *how*, and report any mechanic that cannot be executed as specified.

## The three things the card says a removal must settle

1. ⛔ **Refuse loudly — do not merely stop reading.** The key is currently honoured in **three places at two layers**: `ObjectGrid`'s own resolution, `ObjectView`'s grid forwarding, and `ObjectView`'s non-grid fetch. Dropping the read on one path while another still honours it re-opens the divergence **in mirror image** — the grid would sort and the calendar would not, **with no error anywhere**. ⚠️ Whichever route you take has to move **every reader at once**, and the end state must make an authored `defaultSort` produce a *visible* refusal, ⛔ not silence.
2. **The registries.** ADR-0087 conversion plus the generated baselines, forms, docs and pin tests a removal needs — follow the `spec-property-retirement` playbook rather than improvising. ✅ Name each registry you touched and each you deliberately did not.
3. ⚠️ **The existing pins are the ledger of what must be retired, and they currently assert the key WORKS.** `packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/ObjectView.canonicalTableKeys.test.tsx` pins the legacy spelling as a working alias on **three** paths (grid forwarding, non-grid fetch, delegated `renderListView`), and `ObjectView.sortSink.test.tsx` pins the lowered value. ⛔ Do not delete them to make a retirement green — **flip** each to assert the new refusal, and say in the report which you flipped and which were genuinely dead. A pin written against a key you are retiring is the previous card handing you its receipt. (This exact move was executed correctly on #5725 today, on a pin that was even documented to flip.)

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not inherit

1. ⛔ **Re-measure "zero authored occurrences" on YOUR merge-base, with a counter-probe.** The card measured it on `origin/main` @ `1d9100eeb`; ~30 PRs have landed since. Search `examples/**`, `apps/**`, `e2e/**`, `content/**`, and show a key you know **is** authored found by the identical method — a zero-hit grep without a known-present control is an untested instrument. ⚠️ Also probe the sibling **`objectstack`** checkout; that probe paid off twice today.
2. ⚠️ **Expect two classes of surviving hit that are NOT authoring, and do not confuse them:** the registry/spec-parity ledger in `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`, and prose in `content/docs/plugins/plugin-view.mdx` + `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` describing it as the deprecated half of a pair. ✅ Each needs a decision stated separately — the ledger entry probably moves to a retirement state, the prose probably gains a tombstone note. ⛔ Neither is "an authored occurrence".
3. ⚠️ **The key is already live-for-reading but not-for-writing** — #4648 (maintainer, 2026-08-16) carved `object-grid.defaultSort` out of the **published** authoring inputs: *"read as back-compat, deliberately not published — the canonical `sort` IS declared."* ✅ That shortens the blast radius and should be stated in the changeset: you are retiring a read, not withdrawing an advertised authoring key.
4. ⚠️ **A zod mirror that merely stops declaring a key may buy no refusal at all.** Measured on #6068 today: a plain `z.object` with no `.strict()` **strips** unknown keys rather than rejecting them. ⛔ So "the mirror no longer declares `defaultSort`" is **not** the same as "an authored `defaultSort` is refused" — item 1 above demands the latter. Measure which your change actually produces and say so.
5. **Out of scope, explicitly:** ⛔ this card is **not** about `ObjectViewProps.views[].sort` and its `direction`/`order` spelling mismatch — that is #5293, which stays open and untouched. (Its residue is filed as #6011.)

## Verification

Predict the direction **before** running. ⚠️ **Commit your own edit before you ablate** — measured on #5859 today: a `trap` restore using `git checkout --` reverted the dev's still-uncommitted edit along with the probe's mutation, and `git checkout --` **reported success both times**; the half-change was caught only by an independent `git diff --stat` re-read.

⚠️ **Do any downstream counter-probe at the right layer**: downstream resolves `@object-ui/types` through `exports` to **`dist/`**, ⛔ not `src/` — a source-only mutation leaves the sweep green and reads as "nothing consumes it". Rebuild before reading and re-grep `dist/`.

The retirement's positive evidence is a **refusal that fires**, on **every** one of the three reader paths, each with its own leg. Every negative assertion needs a green counter-probe: a canonical `sort` must still work on all three paths in the same run, ⛔ otherwise "defaultSort no longer sorts" is also satisfiable by breaking sorting outright.

Prove every mutation on disk by grepping injected **and separately** removed text; ⚠️ print the landing site; ⚠️ assert anchor uniqueness before writing; ⚠️ restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a **cwd-independent** command; confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` is empty afterwards.

**Gates by name, with exit codes:** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` and `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-view type-check` (⚠️ hyphenated; echo the script name; distinguish the **unbuilt-closure** red — `Cannot find module @object-ui/...` — from the **missing-`node_modules`** red), root-form vitest over each package touched quoting per-test names, the downstream **prefix-form** sweep with the contract direction **demonstrated** rather than asserted (⚠️ known gotcha, not a finding: `apps/site` and `packages/components` fail until `@object-ui/react-runtime` is built separately), eslint with merge-base delta (⚠️ plain `eslint .`; ⛔ no `--no-inline-config`). Run `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` rather than guessing — ⚠️ **#6073 landed today and widened that gate's notion of a package's source** beyond `/src/`. Changeset **`minor`** for a public-type break; ⛔ never `major`.

⚠️ **Watch for the zero-match pnpm trap** (measured today): a filter that matches nothing prints *"No projects matched the filters"* and exits **0**, reading exactly like a pass. ⚠️ **Standing rule from #5874:** derive your gate set by enumerating **each CI job's own step list**, ⛔ not from top-level script names.

## Deliverable

Draft PR, body with `Fixes #5861`. ⛔ Do not mark ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ no auto-merge — the PM lands it. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — this repo's sanitizer eats them, confirmed twice today) and return it. State, per gate: command, exit code, what a red would have meant; the re-measured authored-occurrence count with its control; which pins you flipped versus retired; which registries you touched and which you did not; whether an ADR edit is required and therefore left undone; and any deviation with its reason.

## PM ruling — **ESCALATE accepted.** No code was the right answer. → `pm:blocked` on objectstack#11805

⛔ This is **not** a REWORK and ⛔ not a re-opening of the ruling. The direction — the key should go — is untouched. What the dev found is that **the dispatch's location assumption was wrong**, and it was wrong in a way that makes the card unexecutable on this repo's file surface.

### The measurement that settles it

`ObjectGridPropsSchema` (`objectstack/packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts:2164`) is a **`strictObject`** that still declares `defaultSort` as a **live authorable key**, publishes it un-retired at `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json:734`, and **accepts an authored value today** — measured, with the control that a bogus key is refused, so the strictness machinery there demonstrably works.

Meanwhile objectui's own mirror (`packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:130`) is a **non-strict `BaseSchema.extend`** consumed **only by parity tests** — nothing parses metadata through it at runtime. ⚠️ **So tombstoning it buys exactly zero refusal.** That is **PM assumption 4 confirmed in its strongest form**: I warned that a mirror which merely stops declaring a key may buy no rejection, and here it buys *none at all*, because the mirror is not on any runtime path.

Dispatch item 1 demanded a **visible refusal, not silence**. The only place that refusal can exist is the upstream `strictObject`. ⇒ The card cannot be executed here.

### Why the two consumer-only routes are correctly rejected

- **B (remove objectui's reads now):** the contract still **accepts** an authored `defaultSort`, so the key becomes **silently dropped** rather than refused. That is item 1's forbidden silence — the ADR-0049 failure mode **relocated, not closed**.
- **C (loud runtime refusal in objectui):** the renderer would refuse a key the pinned contract advertises as legal **in its own describe text** — declared≠enforced *inverted*, which is the class `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` exists to catch. And it cannot move every reader anyway: `plugin-grid` is fenced by in-flight #5729, so `ObjectGrid` would keep honouring the key — **the mirror-image divergence item 1 explicitly forbids.**

✅ And objectui already states this ordering itself: the comment governing the ten ruled object-grid carve-outs in `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` says they *"retire only if `@objectstack/spec` retires the keys upstream."* The dispatch and I both missed that; the dev read it.

### The tripwire already exists, and was measured firing

⚠️ Rather than build new machinery, the dev **proved the existing gate already fires** the day upstream retires the key. Ablation with a **real tombstone** — `page:header.icon`, retired by objectstack#6946 — against the exact assertion `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` uses: leg A (live key) **green**, leg B (real tombstone) **red** with *"expected [ title, subtitle, …(8) ] to include icon"*. Direction predicted before running, observed as predicted.

✅ And the reason a real tombstone was used instead of mutating `node_modules` is exactly right and worth repeating: **pnpm hardlinks the content-addressable store, so editing installed `dist` would have reached every other agent's worktree.** That is a cross-agent hazard in the same family as the shared stash stack.

⇒ Building a second tripwire would be duplicate machinery — the drift `packages/test-support/src/spec-tombstones.ts` exists to end.

### Two corrections to my dispatch, both mine

1. ⚠️ **Assumption 3 was wrong.** I said #4648 made the key "live-for-reading but not-for-writing" and that this **shortens the blast radius**. It does not: #4648 carved it out of the **console registry** inputs, but the key remains published in the spec's **authorable surface** (`ui.json:734`, no `[RETIRED]` tag) and **still accepted by the strictObject**. Not offered as a console input ≠ not a live authorable contract key.
2. ⚠️ **A grep trap I did not warn about:** `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md:537-538` and `:603` document **`CRUDSchema.defaultSort` / `defaultSortOrder`** — a **string** field on a **different carrier**. ⛔ Anyone sweeping `ObjectGridSchema.defaultSort` by grep must not "fix" them. Now on the record for the follow-on.

Also caught **live**, exactly as the dispatch warned: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types^... build` printed *"No projects matched the filters"* and exited **0**. ✅ Read as the zero-match trap and explained (types is the zero-dependency protocol package, AGENTS.md §3), ⛔ not counted as a passing gate.

### Re-measurement, with a working instrument
